test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Pranav borrows a sum of ₹6,23,305 at the rate of 10% per annum simple interest. At the end of the first year, he repays ₹16,390 towards return of principal amount borrowed. If Pranav clears all pending dues at the end of the second year, including interest payment that accrued during the first year, how much does he pay (in ₹) at the end of the second year?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If no repayment was made, the total amount payable after 2 years = Principal + 2 years SI = 6,23,305 + (20% of 6,23,305) = 6,23,305 + 1,24,661 = ₹7,47,966.

Since ₹16,390 is repaid towards the principal after 1 year, this amount is deducted from the final dues.

Additionally, the 10% interest saved on this repaid amount for the 2nd year is also deducted = 10% of 16,390 = ₹1,639.

Total deduction from final amount = 16,390 + 1,639 = ₹18,029.

Final payment = 7,47,966 − 18,029 = ₹7,29,937.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,29,937.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹6,23,305

Rate (R) = 10% p.a. simple interest

Repayment at the end of Year 1 = ₹16,390 (towards principal)

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100
